patches.name: computer-user

files.note: Export the settings schema AND keep it on the default export. On a 0.2.x kernel SettingsForms.schema(entry) reads entry.fiber.runtime.Config (the namespace-registration model was retired and replaced by schema-derived configForms forms). Two separate gates then apply, and a named export alone fails the first: cordis-plugin-loader unwrapExports() collapses the module to its default export before cordis reads plugin.Config (xports = exports.default ?? exports), so with both a named Config and a default object the schema is discarded and describe() omits the namespace. Adding Config to the default object is what actually restores the form; the named binding is kept for tooling.

Mark every Config field volatile(). volatileForm() keeps only fields under a volatile ancestor, so the unmarked upstream schema still projects to undefined and no form is produced even once Config is exported. The live() helper degrades to the plain schema when a schemastery build has no volatile().

Drop the retired settingsScope inject and probe both transport generations instead. Declaring a service no kernel provides parks the client fiber forever in waitingFor, so the whole card vanishes with no error. Now: configForms.get(entryId) on 0.2.x (ConfigFormController already carries the same getSnapshot/subscribe/set/unset surface the Section component uses), settingsScope.bind() on 0.1.x, and no section registered at all when neither exists. Upstream 0.3.7 targets the 0.1.3 kernel, so its browser half still carries this 0.1.x-only inject; this patch supplies the 0.2.x adaptation locally and can be dropped once upstream ships a 0.2.x-compatible client.

patches.summary: Expose Config on the default export (the loader unwraps to default, so a named export alone is dropped), mark its fields volatile, and swap the retired settingsScope inject for a dual-generation configForms probe. files.note: Host side stops importing the retired settingsNamespace/installSettingsSection (ESM link-time SyntaxError on 0.2.x kills the whole plugin tree), stops calling the also-retired ctx.settings.register (0.2.x derives forms from the exported Config schema instead), and marks the schema volatile() so volatileForm() actually projects a card.

Client fiber no longer injects the retired settingsScope service (it parked forever in waitingFor and the settings row silently vanished). Runtime probe prefers configForms (0.2.x) and falls back to settingsScope (0.1.x).

Self-contained 0.1.x-compatible shim for the retired @deepseek-ai/dsh-settings userland (settingsNamespace / installSettingsSection) plus a createSettingsScope helper that rebuilds the retired ctx.settings.register() surface on top of the 0.2.x describe()/update() API. EAC plugins ship self-contained and do not resolve through the kernel package graph, so this file travels with the plugin.
